summary: This packet decomposes Neron models and semistable abelian varieties. It uses four library sources: SGA 7 I Expose IX (a scan read through OCR, with key statements on page images), SGA 7 II Expose XV Theoreme 3.4 (page images), Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves VII.5-VII.7, and Poonen, Rational points on varieties 5.7. It also uses four authorized public copies: Romagny, Neron models of abelian varieties (2011 notes); Lichtenstein, Neron models (Stanford seminar notes); Conrad, Neron models, Tamagawa factors, and Tate-Shafarevich groups (2015 notes); and Raynaud, Specialisation du foncteur de Picard (Publ. IHES 1970, NUMDAM). R11.1 covers the definition, Weil extension, abelian schemes as Neron models and good-reduction criteria, smoothening, the weak Neron property, local existence via birational group laws, Dedekind gluing, base change (unramified versus ramified) and the local invariant-differential line. R11.2 covers component groups, Chevalley decomposition and Tamagawa numbers, elliptic Neron models from minimal models, and the 57C2 example. R11.3 covers semiabelian models, the Galois criterion and the semistable reduction theorem. R11.4 covers Neron models of Jacobians via Raynaud's Picard functor, component groups from multidegrees, the dual-graph character group, Picard-Lefschetz and the component group as a cokernel of the monodromy pairing. R11.5 covers Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich, inertia invariants and local L-factors, and the p-adic criterion. R11.6 covers exactness and uniform semistability. All stages are partial: BLR, the monodromy and orthogonality theorems, the Raynaud extension, conductors, Tate's algorithm and the level-lowering interfaces are unread.

nodes.title: Definition of the Neron model and its formal consequences: uniqueness, products, group structure, A(S) = A(K), and representability of j_* A on smooth schemes
nodes.statement: Let S be a Dedekind scheme with function field K and A_K an abelian variety (more generally X a smooth separated K-scheme of finite type). A Neron model is a smooth, separated S-model A of finite type satisfying the Neron mapping property: every K-morphism u_K : Z_K -> A_K from the generic fibre of a smooth S-scheme Z extends uniquely to an S-morphism Z -> A. If it exists it is unique up to unique isomorphism, the formation commutes with products, the group law extends so A is an S-group scheme, A(S) = A_K(K) (and A(S') = A(K') for quasi-compact etale S' -> S), and A represents the pushforward j_*(A_K) on smooth S-schemes. Separatedness and finite type are not formal consequences of the mapping property. The relative identity component A^0 removes the non-identity components of the finitely many disconnected special fibres. A Neron model is generally not proper.
hypotheses: Conrad Remark 1.6: a smooth K-group of finite type has a Neron model over a DVR iff G(K^sh) is bounded (BLR 1.3/1); no analogue for nontrivial connected semisimple groups over complete R with perfect residue field
Lichtenstein 1.3.9: P^n_R is not the Neron model of P^n_K (automorphisms need not extend)
Lichtenstein 1.3.8: for y^2 = x^3 + pi^2 the smooth locus of the minimal Weierstrass model is "too small" to be the Neron model
proofSteps: Uniqueness: two Neron models dominate each other by the mapping property, and the composites extend the identity, so are the identity by uniqueness.
Products: the mapping property of X x_S X' follows from those of X and X'.
Group law: extend m_K : A_K x A_K -> A_K using the product property; identities extend by uniqueness.
A(S) = A_K(K): apply the mapping property to Z = S (and to etale S').
acceptance: Verify that a Neron model of an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction is not proper (roadmap check).
Keep identity component, component group and the whole group scheme distinct in every statement.

nodes.title: Weil's extension theorem (BLR 4.4/1): an S-rational map from a smooth S-scheme to a smooth separated S-group, defined in codimension 1, is defined everywhere
nodes.statement: Let S be a normal noetherian scheme, Z a smooth S-scheme and G a smooth separated S-group scheme. If an S-rational map f : Z --> G is defined in codimension <= 1, then it is defined everywhere. S-rational maps are classes of morphisms on S-dense open subschemes; for Y smooth and separated a rational map has a maximal domain of definition (2.1.2), and definedness descends along faithfully flat maps (2.1.3, BLR 2.5/5).

nodes.title: Lichtenstein Proposition 2.2.4 and Corollary 2.2.7, SGA 7 IX 2.2.9: an abelian scheme is the Neron model of its generic fibre; good reduction iff the Neron model is an abelian scheme iff A^0_k is proper iff inertia acts trivially on T_l
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind domain (or DVR) with fraction field K and A an abelian scheme over R with generic fibre A_K; then A is the Neron model of A_K. For an abelian variety A_K over the fraction field of a DVR with Neron model A, the following are equivalent: (i) A_K has good reduction (some abelian scheme over R has generic fibre A_K); (ii) A is an abelian scheme; (iii) A^0_k is proper; (iv) A is proper over R; and (SGA 7 IX 2.2.9, for l != char k) the Tate module T_l(A) is unramified, i.e. the inertia group acts trivially on T_l(A(Kbar)). An abelian scheme with generic fibre A_K is unique up to unique isomorphism.
hypotheses: The step (iii) => (ii) uses: a smooth R-scheme with geometrically connected generic fibre and proper special fibre is proper (Serre-Tate, Lemma 3 of section 1, cited; Conrad cites EGA IV 15.7.10)
SGA 7 IX 2.2.9 lists further equivalent conditions (A_s abelian, A^0_s abelian, the l^nu-torsion unramified); its proof was not read
proofSteps: Proposition 2.2.4: given smooth Y and f : Y_K -> A_K, spread out f over a neighbourhood of the generic point of S (Lemma 2.2.5).

At the generic points eta of closed fibres, O_{Y,eta} is a DVR, so the valuative criterion for the proper A extends f to Spec O_{Y,eta}, hence to a neighbourhood; glue by separatedness to an S-rational map defined in codimension 1.
Weil's extension theorem extends it to all of Y; uniqueness follows from separatedness.
Corollary 2.2.7: (i) => (ii) by uniqueness of Neron models; (iii) => (ii) since A^0 is proper (Serre-Tate lemma), a subgroup scheme, hence an abelian scheme and the Neron model, so A^0 = A.

nodes.title: Romagny Theorem 2.4.2 (Neron-Raynaud): finitely many permissible blow-ups make every point of a given set E of R^sh-points lift to the smooth locus
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR, A a flat R-scheme of finite type with smooth generic fibre and E a subset of A(R^sh). Neron's defect delta(a) is the length of the torsion submodule of a^*Omega^1_{A/R}, and delta(A, E) = max over a in E (finite, BLR 3.3/3); delta(A, E) = 0 iff E lies in A^sm(R^sh) (Lemma 2.2.2). There is a finite sequence of E-permissible blow-ups A' -> A (centres geometrically reduced closed subschemes of the special fibre, dense in the specializations of E, meeting them in the smooth locus where Omega^1 is locally free) such that each point of E lifts uniquely to a smooth point of A'. Applied to E = A_0(R^sh) for a proper flat model A_0, it gives a smoothening A_1 -> A_0 whose smooth locus is a weak Neron model.
hypotheses: Imported, proof omitted in the source: Lemma 2.3.2 (Neron, Raynaud): blowing up the centre Y^i strictly lowers delta at points of E^i with singular specialization (BLR 3.3/5); boundedness of delta (BLR 3.3/3)
Existence of a proper flat model uses Nagata compactification (Conrad, Deligne's notes) and schematic closure
proofSteps: Lemma 2.2.2: if delta(a) = 0, a^*Omega^1 is free of rank d_K; by semicontinuity of fibre dimensions the special fibre is smooth at a_k (EGA IV 17.15.5); conversely smoothness gives local freeness.
Canonical partition: Y^1 = closure of specializations of E, U^1 its smooth part where Omega^1 is locally free, E^1 = points specializing into U^1; iterate on the rest to get E = E^1 u ... u E^t.
Induction on delta(A, E) + t(A, E): blow up Y^t (E^t-permissible), which lowers delta on E^t (Lemma 2.3.2); by induction smoothen E^t; the remaining partition has length t - 1; induct again.
acceptance: Record the omitted Lemma 2.3.2 as the load-bearing import of the local existence theorem.
Check that the process uses R^sh-points, i.e. the Neron model is first built after strict henselization and then descended.

nodes.title: Romagny Proposition 3.2.1: a weak Neron model extends K-rational maps from smooth R-schemes to R-rational maps
nodes.statement: Let A be a weak Neron model of A_K over a DVR R (a smooth separated finite-type model with A(R^sh) = A_K(K^sh), equivalently the extension property for etale test schemes). Then every K-rational map u_K : Z_K --> A_K from the generic fibre of a smooth R-scheme Z extends uniquely to an R-rational map Z --> A. Conversely, a smooth separated finite-type model with this property is a weak Neron model.
hypotheses: Weak Neron models are not unique: their special fibres contain extraneous components
Uses constructibility of images and Zariski's Main Theorem-type spreading out of local isomorphisms
proofSteps: Reduce to Z with irreducible special fibre and u_K everywhere defined.

Let Gamma be the schematic closure of the graph of u_K in Z x A; every k^s-point of Z_k lifts to an R^sh-point whose image extends into A (weak Neron property), so the image of Gamma_k -> Z_k contains a dense open set.

At the generic point eta of Z_k, O_{Z,eta} is a DVR dominated by O_{Gamma,xi} with the same generic fibre, so they coincide; spread out to an isomorphism of open neighbourhoods and compose with the projection to A.
acceptance: Check the use of R^sh-points: the argument needs every k^s-point of the smooth special fibre to lift.

nodes.title: Romagny section 4, Lichtenstein 1.3.10 and 3.6.1, Poonen 5.7.25: removing non-minimal components of a weak Neron model gives an R-birational group law whose Weil solution is the Neron model, of finite type
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR with fraction field K and A_K an abelian variety of dimension d. Then A_K has a Neron model over R, of finite type (and quasi-projective, by Raynaud). Construction: let A_2 be a weak Neron model (smooth locus of a smoothening of a proper flat model), omega a left-invariant (hence also right-invariant, Lemma 4.1.1) volume form normalized so that the minimum of its orders along special-fibre components is 0, and A_3 the open subscheme obtained by removing the non-minimal components. Then omega generates Omega^d_{A_3/R} (Lemma 4.1.2); multiplication extends to an R-birational group law on A_3 (Theorem 4.2.1); Weil's theorem on birational group laws gives a smooth separated R-group scheme A_4 of finite type containing an R-dense open of A_3 and extending the law; and A_4 satisfies the Neron mapping property (Proposition 4.2.2).
hypotheses: Imported: Weil's extension theorem for R-birational group laws (the "previous lecture" of the summer school; BLR 5.1/5 for A_3 embedding into A_4), Weil's extension theorem for rational maps into group schemes (BLR 4.4/1), the invariant volume form (BLR 4.2), Zariski's Main Theorem (EGA IV 8.12.10)
Remark 4.2.3: quasi-projectivity is Raynaud, Faisceaux amples (LNM 119), Theorem VIII.2, not read
Poonen Theorem 5.7.25 states existence and finite type with proof by citation (Artin 1986, BLR 1.3 Corollary 2)
proofSteps: Lemma 4.1.1: c_x^*omega = chi(x) omega defines a character A_K -> G_m, trivial because A_K is proper, so left-invariant forms are right-invariant.
Lemma 4.1.2: omega extends over the normal A_2 and does not vanish in codimension 1 on A_3, hence nowhere.

Theorem 4.2.1: extend m_K to m : A_3 x A_2 --> A_2 (weak Neron property); phi(x, y) = (x, xy) preserves the pulled-back form, which forces the order at image components to be 0, so m maps into A_3; phi is etale (determinant of differentials is an isomorphism) and an isomorphism generically, hence an open immersion (Zariski's Main Theorem); similarly for (xy, y).
Apply Weil's theorem on birational group laws to get A_4.
Proposition 4.2.2: extend tau_K(z, x) = u_K(z) x to Z x A_3 --> A_3, view as a rational map to A_4, extend everywhere by Weil's theorem for group schemes, and restrict to the unit section.

nodes.title: Lichtenstein 2.3.1-2.3.4: Neron models over a Dedekind base are obtained by gluing an abelian scheme over a dense open with the finitely many local Neron models
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and X a smooth separated K-scheme of finite type. An R-scheme of finite type X with generic fibre X is a Neron model iff X x_S Spec O_{S,s} is a Neron model over O_{S,s} for every closed point s (Lemma 2.3.3, BLR 1.2/4). X has a Neron model over R iff there are a dense open S', a Neron model over S' and Neron models over O_{S,s} for the finitely many s outside S' (Proposition 2.3.2). Hence every abelian variety A over K has a global Neron model over Spec R, which is an abelian scheme over the open subscheme where A has good reduction (Theorem 2.3.4). Neron models over an open cover glue (Exercise 2.3.1).
hypotheses: Spreading out finitely presented schemes and morphisms from local rings to neighbourhoods (Lemma 2.2.5) is used throughout

For the finitely many closed points outside U, take local Neron models (Theorem 1.3.10) and spread them out to neighbourhoods S_i agreeing with the abelian scheme over S_i intersect U.
Glue to a smooth separated finite-type model, and check the mapping property stalk-locally (Lemma 2.3.3).

nodes.title: Neron models commute with etale base change and extensions of ramification index 1 (descending from R^sh), but not with ramified base change
nodes.statement: The formation of Neron models commutes with etale base change (Lichtenstein 1.4.3) and with localization, completion, henselization and strict henselization (Conrad, property 2). For a local extension R -> R' of DVRs with ramification index 1, a smooth K-group G has a Neron model over R iff G_{K'} has one over R', and then it is the base change (6.2.2, BLR 7.2/1); Neron models descend from R' inside R^sh (6.2.1, BLR 6.5/4). A smooth R-group G of finite type is the Neron model of its generic fibre iff G(R^sh) -> G(K^sh) is bijective (6.1.1, BLR 7.1/1). Ramified base change fails: y^2 = x^3 + p over Q_p (p not dividing 6) has additive reduction but good reduction over Q_p(p^{1/6}), so the base change of the non-proper Neron model is not the proper Neron model; for split multiplicative reduction the special fibre G_m x Z/nZ with n = -ord(j) becomes G_m x Z/neZ after ramification index e (Conrad Example 2.2). If A has semistable reduction everywhere, base change to any finite separable extension induces isomorphisms of relative identity components (Conrad Theorem 3.7, BLR 7.4).

proofSteps: Etale base change: for smooth Y' over R' etale over R, Y' is smooth over R, so the mapping property over R gives the one over R' (1.4.3).
Ramified counterexample: if the base change of the non-proper model were the proper Neron model over R', properness would descend along the faithfully flat R -> R' (4.1.9).

nodes.statement: For a smooth R-group scheme of relative dimension d the sheaf Omega^d is invertible and locally generated by an invariant form (BLR 4.2). For the Neron model A of A over a complete DVR R with finite residue field and fraction field F, the R-line Omega^top_{A/R} inside the F-line Omega^top_{A/F} is preferred; a generator omega is unique up to R^x and the measure |omega| mu^d on A(F) is a canonical Haar measure. nodes.title: Component group Phi_s = A_s/A^0_s as a finite etale group, rational versus geometric points, Tamagawa numbers, and the Chevalley decomposition 1 -> T x U -> A^0_k -> B -> 1
nodes.statement: For the Neron model A of an abelian variety over a Dedekind scheme and a closed point s, the component group Phi_s = A_s/A^0_s is a finite etale k(s)-group, viewed as Phi_s(k(s)^sep) with its Galois action. A_s(k(s)) -> Phi_s(k(s)) need not be surjective (obstruction in H^1(k(s), A^0_s)), but it is for finite k(s) (Lang). The Tamagawa number is c(A) = #Phi(k). Over a perfect residue field, A^0_k is uniquely an extension 1 -> T x U -> A^0_k -> B -> 1 with T a torus, U smooth connected unipotent and B an abelian variety (Chevalley); the toric, unipotent and abelian ranks are dim T, dim U, dim B. For l != char k, 0 -> V_l(T) -> V_l(A^0_k) -> V_l(B) -> 0 is exact (the unipotent part drops out).

nodes.title: Lichtenstein 4.1-4.3, Poonen 5.7.30, Silverman VII.5-VII.6: E^sm of the minimal regular model is the Neron model, W^sm of a minimal Weierstrass model is its identity component, and reduction types and the filtration agree with the scheme data
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR with fraction field K and E/K an elliptic curve with minimal regular proper model E, minimal Weierstrass model W and Neron model N. Then E^sm -> N is an isomorphism and W^sm -> N^0 is an isomorphism. For K complete with finite residue field, the reduction map r : E(K) = N(R) -> N_k(k) defines E(K)^1 = ker r contained in E(K)^0 = r^{-1}(N^0_k(k)), with E(K)^0/E(K)^1 = N^0_k(k) and E(K)/E(K)^0 = Phi_E(k). Good, multiplicative and additive reduction (smooth, nodal, cuspidal minimal Weierstrass reduction; Silverman VII.5.1: v(Delta) = 0; v(Delta) > 0, v(c_4) = 0; v(Delta), v(c_4) > 0) coincide with N^0_k being an elliptic curve, G_m, or G_a over the algebraic closure. In the split multiplicative case (Kodaira I_n, v(j) = -n) the special fibre of N is the smooth part of a loop of n rational curves, N^0_k = G_m, and E(K)/E_0(K) is cyclic of order -v(j) (Silverman VII.6.1); otherwise it has order at most 4.

nodes.title: SGA 7 IX 3.2-3.4 and Conrad 3.3-3.7: semistable reduction means semiabelian identity components; any smooth separated model with semiabelian fibres is an open subgroup of the Neron model, stable under base change on identity components
nodes.statement: Let S be a locally noetherian regular integral scheme of dimension 1 with function field K, A_K an abelian variety and A its Neron model. The following are equivalent (3.2): (i) for every s in S, A^0_s has unipotent rank 0, i.e. is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus; (ii) there is a smooth separated S-group scheme G of finite type extending A_K whose fibres have unipotent rank 0. If G is as in (ii), the morphism G -> A is an isomorphism onto an open subgroup, hence an isomorphism on identity components. A_K then has semistable reduction (Definition 3.4). For a dominant S' -> S of the same type, A x_S S' -> A' (Neron model over S') is an open immersion, an isomorphism on identity components (3.3), though not in general on component groups. Equivalently (Conrad Theorem 3.7, BLR 7.4) a semi-abelian scheme extending A_K is the identity component of its Neron model.

nodes.title: SGA 7 IX Proposition 3.5 and Corollaries 3.5.2, 3.8: semistable reduction iff inertia acts unipotently of echelon 2 on T_l, iff it acts unipotently
nodes.statement: Let S be a trait (henselian after localization), A_K an abelian variety over K and l a prime different from the residue characteristic. The following are equivalent: (i) A_K has semistable reduction; (ii) in the notation of 2.5.3, V = V^f (the fixed part) is equal to the orthogonal of the toric part; (iv) the inertia group I acts unipotently of echelon 2 on U = T_l(A(Kbar)), i.e. there is an I-stable submodule U' with I acting trivially on U' and on U/U'. These are also equivalent to (v) I acts through its maximal pro-l quotient Z_l(1) and a topological generator g satisfies (1 - g)^2 = 0 on U (3.5.2), and to (vi) I acts unipotently on T_l(A(Kbar)) (3.8). The conditions depend only on the Q_l-representation, are stable under base change of traits, and pass to abelian subvarieties, quotients and isogenous varieties.
hypotheses: The proof uses the orthogonality theorem IX 2.4: the toric part T_l(A)^t is the intersection of the fixed part T_l(A)^I with the orthogonal of the fixed part of the dual, for the canonical pairing; 2.4 is proved via biextensions (Exposes VII-VIII), not read
Corollaire 3.8 uses that a unipotent algebraic group in characteristic 0 is connected, so a finite-index subgroup has the same unipotence echelon
The OCR of condition (iii) is illegible; it was not transcribed

By the orthogonality theorem 2.4, (ii) is equivalent to (iii).
(iv) means I acts trivially on U^t = V^f, which by duality means it acts trivially on V, i.e. (ii).
(v): an unipotent continuous action of a profinite group on an l-adic space factors through a pro-l group, hence through Z_l(1).

nodes.title: SGA 7 IX Theoreme 3.6 (Grothendieck): after a finite Galois extension an abelian variety acquires semistable reduction over the normalized Dedekind base; Conrad 3.5: the field K(A[l]) (A[4] for l = 2) suffices
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected regular noetherian scheme of dimension 1 with function field K and A_K an abelian variety. There is a finite Galois extension K' of K such that A_{K'} has semistable reduction on the normalization S' of S in K'. Over a DVR one can take K' = K(A[l]) for any prime l != char k (K(A[4]) when l = 2), so semistable reduction everywhere is achieved after splitting the 15-torsion, with [K' : K] dividing #GL_{2g}(Z/15Z) for g = dim A. For elliptic curves (Silverman VII.5.4) additive reduction becomes good or multiplicative after a finite extension, while good and multiplicative reduction are stable.

nodes.title: Raynaud 1970 Theoremes 8.1.4 and 8.2.1, SGA 7 IX Theoreme 12.1: for a proper flat curve X over a trait with factorial local rings, P/E is a Neron group, and when the generic fibre is geometrically integral P^0 = Pic^0_{X/S} is the identity component of the Neron model of the Jacobian
nodes.statement: Let S be a trait, f : X -> S proper and flat with fibres of dimension 1 and factorial local rings (e.g. X regular). Let P = Pic_{X/S}, E the schematic closure of the unit section and Q = P/E. Then Q_S (the relevant part of Q) is a Neron S-group of finite type if k(s) is perfect or delta (the gcd of the total multiplicities of the components of X_s) is prime to the characteristic exponent (Raynaud 8.1.4). The following are related by (i) => (ii) => (iii) => (iv) <=> (v) <=> (vi) <=> (vii) => (viii): (i) delta = 1; (ii) the generic fibre has a divisor of degree 1; (iii) there is a universal invertible sheaf; (iv) X is cohomologically flat and d' = 1; (v) P is representable; (vi) P^0 is representable; (vii) P^0 is separated; (viii) d' = 1; all equivalent if delta = d' (e.g. factorial local rings and perfect k(s)) (Raynaud 8.2.1). In SGA 7 IX 12.1 form (S strictly local, f_*O_X = O_S, factorial local rings, d = 1): Q = P/E is a smooth separated Neron group, 0 -> A -> Q -deg-> Z -> 0 with A the Neron model of the Jacobian of the generic fibre, and P^0 -> A^0 is an isomorphism. Hence N(J)^0 = Pic^0_{X/S} when the gcd of the geometric multiplicities of the non-smooth fibres is 1 (Conrad Example 2.3).
hypotheses: Raynaud's proof uses the Brauer group of the strictly henselian generic point (killed by delta; zero for perfect residue field) and the factoriality to extend invertible sheaves; Remarque 8.1.5 notes that this route to Neron models of Jacobians is less elementary than Neron's and uses Abhyankar's desingularization

nodes.title: Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich: an abelian variety has good reduction iff T_l is unramified (Lichtenstein 5.2.1 with proof; SGA 7 IX 2.2.9; Silverman VII.7.1-7.3 for elliptic curves), with isogeny invariance
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR with fraction field K and perfect residue field k of characteristic p, A an abelian variety over K and l != p. Then A has good reduction iff T_l(A) is unramified (inertia acts trivially). Consequently good reduction is invariant under isogeny and passes to abelian subvarieties and quotients (Lichtenstein 5.2.9; Silverman VII.7.2), and for elliptic curves E has potential good reduction iff inertia acts on T_l(E) through a finite quotient (Silverman VII.7.3). Silverman's elliptic version: good reduction iff E[m] is unramified for all (or infinitely many) m prime to char k iff T_l(E) is unramified for some (all) l != char k.
hypotheses: Lichtenstein's proof uses: A[l^n](K_s)^I = A[l^n](K^nr) = A[l^n](R^sh) = A_k[l^n](k_s) (Lemma 5.2.3, with BLR 7.3/3 for the last bijection); Chevalley's structure theorem over perfect k; and Corollary 2.2.7 (proper identity component implies good reduction)
Silverman's proof uses the finiteness of E(K^nr)/E_0(K^nr) (VII.6.2, from the Neron model or Tate's algorithm, cited) and injectivity of prime-to-p torsion into the reduction (VII.3.1)
Perfect residue field is assumed in Lichtenstein section 5.2 and in Silverman chapter VII
proofSteps: (i) => (ii): if A has good reduction, A_k is an abelian variety, so A_k[l^n](k_s) has rank 2d, and by Lemma 5.2.3 so does A[l^n](K_s)^I; hence inertia acts trivially.
(ii) => (i): write A^0_k as an extension of B by T x U; A^0_k[l^n](k_s) is free of rank dim T + 2 dim B and has index dividing c(A) in A_k[l^n](k_s).
If T_l is unramified, A_k[l^n](k_s) has order l^{2n dim A} for large n; comparing, 2 dim A = dim T + 2 dim B, and with dim T + dim U + dim B = dim A this forces T = U = 0.
So A^0_k is proper and A has good reduction (Corollary 2.2.7).

nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) with absolute ramification index e < p - 1, and 0 -> A' -> A -> A'' -> 0 an exact sequence of abelian varieties over K. If A has good reduction then so do A' and A'', and the sequence of Neron models (abelian schemes) is exact: A -> A'' is smooth surjective and A' -> A is a closed immersion identifying A' with the kernel (Lichtenstein 6.3.1, BLR 7.5/4, proved with Raynaud's results on group schemes of type (p, ..., p)). If A merely has semi-abelian reduction, the sequence of Neron models is still left exact and A', A'' have semi-abelian reduction. For consumers requiring everywhere-semistable reduction of g-dimensional abelian varieties, a finite extension of degree dividing #GL_{2g}(Z/15Z) suffices (Conrad, after Theorem 3.5), and after semistability all further change of the Neron model under finite separable extension is concentrated in the component groups (Theorem 3.7).
